findings.title: Zero-length date overrides are never recognized as equal
findings.body: `dayjs(...) === dayjs(...)` compares two distinct Dayjs object references, so it is always false even when `start` and `end` represent the same instant. A zero-length override, which represents an unavailable date/time, therefore falls through to the range checks; notably the slot beginning exactly at the override instant is treated as available. This allows bookings during an explicitly blocked override. Compare the instants with `isSame` (or timestamps) instead.

findings.title: Fixed hosts with multiple working-hour ranges are checked as an intersection
findings.body: The working-hours check returns unavailable as soon as the slot is outside any matching range because it uses `find` with an out-of-range predicate. For a common split schedule such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, a 10:00 slot is outside the second range and a 14:00 slot is outside the first, so every slot is rejected for the fixed host. The check must instead accept a slot if it fits at least one applicable working-hour range.

findings.title: Working-hours validation ignores the event duration
findings.body: Both `start` and `end` are calculated from `slotStartTime`, so the new fixed-host working-hours validation only verifies that the slot start is before the end of availability. For example, a 60-minute event starting at 16:30 is accepted for a host whose hours end at 17:00. This can expose round-robin slots that the fixed host cannot actually attend; `end` needs to include `eventLength`.

findings.title: Multiple date-override ranges on one day are treated as mutually exclusive
findings.body: The callback passed to `dateOverrides.find` returns true when a slot is outside any one override range. Consequently, if a host has two availability override windows on the same date, a slot inside the first window is outside the second and is rejected. Date override ranges should be combined as a union: the slot should be accepted when it fits at least one override range, and rejected only when it fits none.

findings.title: No regression test covers the fixed-host round-robin behavior claimed by this PR
findings.body: The added test only exercises a single-host event's override under two nearby time zones. It does not create a ROUND_ROBIN event with a fixed host and a loose host, nor verify that an override or normal fixed-host availability removes otherwise available loose-host slots. The new `checkIfIsAvailable` path is only used for that host filtering and currently has range-handling defects that this missing scenario would have caught.
